mbm-2326.quote: I juggle two yellow beanbags and one real lemon. My sister threw me an orange on the last beat. I caught all four and nearly bit a beanbag.

mbm-2327.clue: I take sunrise home in a jam jar.
mbm-2327.quote: After my dawn paddle I stood a jar on the dock. Pink sky and lake both fit. I put the lid on. My niece still checks it for clouds.

mbm-2328.quote: I clipped a brass bell to my climbing bag so Mum could hear me from the picnic table. Now she climbs too. I hear her bell on the next route over.

mbm-2329.clue: We give the pigeons a head start.
mbm-2329.quote: In each new city I sketch a park bench and the first pigeon that lands on it. Dad can tell Paris from home but he swears it's the same pigeon.

mbm-2330.clue: The mitten makes one run a year.
mbm-2330.quote: Grandpa's wool mitten is huge on me. On the season's last ski run I button it to my jacket. It flaps like he's waving to everyone on the lift.

mbm-2331.clue: I get a different medal every Tuesday.
mbm-2331.quote: Our running group takes turns picking a finish line. This week it was a plum tree. We picked our medals and ate them on the walk back.

mbm-2332.quote: My first dog slept on my blue quilt. I sewed his old collar around a pale patch when he got old. I still reach for that moon when the house gets quiet.

mbm-2333.clue: I leave the paddle by the microphone.
mbm-2333.quote: I recorded a kayak trip for my aunt when her knee kept her ashore. Her favorite part was my paddle dripping on the dock. She says it means cocoa's coming.

mbm-2334.clue: Our sunflower has an inside joke.
mbm-2334.quote: I asked my brothers to draw petals for my quilt. One drew teaspoons. His sunflower catches all the crumbs in the middle of our Sunday picnic.

mbm-2335.clue: I saved the part of the apron nobody saves.
mbm-2335.quote: Mum twisted her apron tie when she waited for bread to rise. I stitched the curled bit into our family quilt. My sister knew whose it was by touch.

mbm-2336.clue: The bench was my favorite exhibit.
mbm-2336.quote: I spent hours drawing a museum bench shaped like a whale. The guard showed me a tiny tail carved under the seat. I turned the page and stayed another hour.

mbm-2337.clue: I keep the heaviest book for the smallest flowers.
mbm-2337.quote: My field guide is full of clover from places I've read it. In the chapter about oaks is a four-leaf one. I haven't needed a bookmark there since.

mbm-2338.clue: I order the same bottle after every bath.
mbm-2338.quote: My uncle and I get cold milk after the hot spring. We tap the empty bottles, then look at the mountain through them to see whose is taller.

mbm-2339.clue: I drew my landing circle around a beetle.
mbm-2339.quote: After my first skydive I found a little green beetle on my boot. I drew it beside the altitude in my log. Its flight was quieter than mine.

mbm-2340.clue: My paddle knows Mum's favorite song.
mbm-2340.quote: I tap the gunwale twice at every bend. Mum sings the next line from the bow of the canoe. We took the long way home to get to the good verse.

mbm-2341.clue: The torn corner was my best cut.
mbm-2341.quote: My nephew ripped one square of my paper banner. I made the gap into a kite tail and cut the rest to match. In the courtyard a whole sky took off.

mbm-2342.clue: My best hold is named for a sandwich.
mbm-2342.quote: I missed the handhold till someone called it grilled cheese. Now I spot two yellow triangular holds from the floor. The climbing gym was hungry when I finished.

mbm-2343.clue: One mile is three good jokes.
mbm-2343.quote: My cousin cycles beside me on my runs. She tells the setups from her saddle and makes me catch up for the punchlines. I ran a personal best for one about a frog.

mbm-2344.quote: I sewed a clear pocket inside my concert jacket to show Dad's old ticket. When I turn back the lapel I can almost hear the band through the door.

mbm-2345.clue: I like the long way round our table.
mbm-2345.quote: My chess partner uses a wheelchair. We chalked a wide lane round the park board so kids wouldn't park their scooters there. They added checkered flags for the endgame.

mbm-2346.clue: We have one commercial break in the dark.
mbm-2346.quote: At pajama night we switch off the lamp during ads to see who can make the best shadow with a slipper. My sister's rabbit has an excellent rubber sole.

mbm-2347.clue: That feather made it round the cape.
mbm-2347.quote: A feather stuck to the bow of my kayak. It rode two waves and a narrow channel. I put it on my map at home so it got credit for the trip.

mbm-2348.clue: I borrowed my coat from a scarecrow.
mbm-2348.quote: I modeled for drawing class in a huge patched coat. Each artist invented a different person who used to wear it. Looking at those sketches I wanted to meet every one.

mbm-2349.quote: I turn the nick in one wooden clave toward my palm. When my cousins play son and the rhythm settles in, that notch fits my hand like an old doorstep key.

mbm-2350.clue: I can tell winter from summer by touch.
mbm-2350.quote: I made a porch quilt with a square for each month. July is a thin picnic shirt. December's a wool scarf. My eyes can stay shut through the whole year.
